records.issue_text: [BUG] The negative assertion for the webauthn form is wrapped in try/catch (Exception), so it can never fail: driver.findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the form is absent (the expected case), and when the form IS present the assertThat(..., nullValue()) failure is an AssertionError, which is also caught by catch (Exception) and swallowed, making the whole check a no-op guard. The test 'reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey' stays green even if the webauthn form is wrongly rendered during password-only re-authentication (and on initial login), so a regression that re-introduces the passkey button for users without passkeys ships undetected.
records.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test wraps `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` in `try { ... } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. However, the finding claims the assertion failure is swallowed because it’s caught by `catch (Exception)`. That mechanism is contradicted by Java’s type hierarchy: `assertThat` failures throw `AssertionError` (an `Error`), not an `Exception`, so it is **not** caught by `catch (Exception)`. records.issue_text: [BUG] The guard for filling WebAuthn context data in authenticate() was silently inverted: the old code called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when the user was NOT yet selected (initial login), while the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null, so the initial-login path (user == null) no longer calls fillContextForm from authenticate(). First-visit username/password pages under a UsernamePasswordForm execution get their WebAuthn conditional-UI form data populated only if some other call site (e.g. challenge() or lazy form rendering) compensates; if it does not, the passkey autofill UI disappears on first login — a regression outside the PR's stated re-authentication objective with no test asserting the initial-page setup comes from this code path.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication (user already set in the auth context, e.g. prompt=login step-up), the UsernameForm no longer short-circuits to success when conditional passkeys are enabled, so the username entry form is rendered for an already-identified user with no visible enforcement in this diff that a subsequently submitted/selected identity must match the already-authenticated user. A step-up re-authentication session (e.g., admin console 'confirm identity' prompt) can be completed with a different username/passkey identity than the user the session was re-authenticating; any consumer relying on re-auth asserting the same principal (required actions, elevated admin operations) gets a silently switched identity. Admins configuring passkeys realms are bitten whenever the flow is used for step-up.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication, fillContextForm(context) is invoked twice for the same challenge — once in authenticate() and again inside challenge() — because both now fire when the user is set. The next change to fillContextForm's side effects (form attributes, authenticator lookup, session notes) has to reason about being applied twice per request; today it duplicates WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction and credential lookups on every re-authentication page render, a hot-path doubling of the DB-backed credential query.
